{{Quote|Let the power of my mind guide you! Yours is the ''muscle'', but mine is the ''will''!|[[Cartariun]], exerting his influence over the [[Irrukiine]]|<ref name="XWRS">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Requiem for a Rogue]]''</ref>}}
'''Qâzoi Kyantuska''' (translated as '''Suppress Thought''' in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] and otherwise known as '''control mind''') was a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith sorcery/Legends|magical]] [[Force power/Legends|ability]] that made the wielder effectively able to control and influence the minds of anyone they chose.

==Description==
Employers of Qâzoi Kyantuska were capable of using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to telepathically dominate a single mind, or a multitude of individuals simultaneously. There did not appear to be any incantation or gestures required, as known users were shown to have simply been in the presence of their victims. The affected were seemingly in a trance, hypnotically paralyzed and unable to control their own faculties. Should the conjurer choose, the victim could end their own life against their own will. If the caster was in direct physical contact with an individual, they could tap directly into the individual's mind, and force them into whatever action they so desired.<ref name="TSW3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 3]]</ref>

==History==
[[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith Acolyte]] [[Satal Keto/Legends|Satal Keto]] displayed a physically taxing yet working mastery of mind control. With his power, Keto telepathically took command of his [[Krath/Legends|Krath]] [[CX-133 Chaos fighter|chaos fighters]] and turned them into living weapons. These [[Death/Legends|suicidal]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] all met their demise under Keto's hypnotic will, using their ships to [[Ramming/Legends|crash]] into the opposing [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Republic Navy/Legends|forces]].<ref name="DLOTS2">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 2]]</ref>

Perhaps the most famous use of control mind was by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]]. During the [[Trial of Ulic Qel-Droma|trial]] of his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]], Kun stormed the hearing and mentally "froze" the entire assembly, except for [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Sidrona]] and the Jedi present. Kun grabbed the Chancellor by his head, and when Kun's [[Sith talisman/Legends|Sith amulet]] began to resonate with the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], the Chancellor's words were those of Kun&mdash;he was exerting his psychic control via direct physical contact. Sidrona was forced to preach Sith ideology, then when Kun was finished, he released his grip on the Chancellor, who then slumped down dead on the floor.<ref name="TSW3" />

The [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]], also known as Vitiate or by his birth name, Tenebrae, was a prominent figure with one of the most potent manifestations of this ability. Vitiate utilized Qâzoi Kyantuska to dominate the will of influential individuals and bend them to his dark side agenda, even making [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak|Malak]] his thralls for a time.<ref name="Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref>

The [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Cartariun]] found a [[Sith Temple (Malrev IV)|Sith Temple]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Malrev IV]] where he stayed isolated for a number of [[Standard year/Legends|years]], learning to harness the power of the dark side through Sith magic. Though he eventually drove himself into madness, he gained enough knowledge of Sith magic to exert his will over the native [[Irrukiine]]. He was murdered however, by [[Girov Dza'tey]] who sought his dark power for himself.<ref name="XWRS" />

Thousands of years later, Joruus C'baoth would do something similar to what Keto did, taking control over a ship's crew to shoot up an enemy that hit his ship.<ref name="TSW3" /><ref name="Dark Force Rising">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref> Later in Thrawn's campaign, the insane clone made [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Captain Pellaeon]] obey him, then later briefly dominated ''[[Chimaera/Legends|Chimaera's]]'' 37,000 souls (except those inside a Force-void) in a fit of fury.<ref name="The Last Command">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref>
